messages:
maya: Heads-up — seeing gaps in trace propagation through the trace-gateway to runtimes in eu-west this morning. Correlates with a spike in GPU tail latency and SLO alerts around 09:10 UTC. :eyes:
juan: Got an alert link? can you paste a sample trace id / logs?
maya: monitoring-bot posted the alert earlier: 
monitoring-bot: ALERT: inference.tail_latency_p99 > 850ms (eu-west) — count=37 in 5m — routed to eng-sre
maya: sample request id: req_6f2b3a. From the gateway logs we see the incoming trace header present, but the runtime spans don't have the same trace id. Gateway log snippet: 
```
[09:07:12] incoming headers: {"traceparent":"00-4bf92f3577b34da6a3ce929d0e0e4736-00f067aa0ba902b7-01","x-request-id":"req_6f2b3a"}
[09:07:12] forwarded headers to runtime: {"x-request-id":"req_6f2b3a"}
```
maya: note: traceparent is missing in forwarded headers above.
liam: that's bad — looks like the gateway is dropping traceparent before calling the runtime. Did we change the Envoy sidecar or ALB config recently?
sasha: there was a gateway deploy ~08:55 by @deploy-bot that touched the outbound proxy routing.
deploy-bot: deploy 2026-02-21T08:55:12Z: trace-gateway v2.3.7 -> v2.4.0 (outbound-proxy fix). rollout finished.
juan: ALB vs envoy — remember ALB can strip certain headers if they contain colons or exceed length, but traceparent is standard. More likely Envoy filter or header sanitizer. Can you grep the gateway config for header_rewrite/preserve?
maya: checking config now. gateway config has: 
```
http_filters:
  - name: envoy.filters.http.header_to_metadata
  - name: envoy.filters.http.router
request_headers_to_remove: ["x-envoy-external-address"]
# no explicit preserve list
```
maya: nothing obvious.
liam: We also saw region-only effect (eu-west). US clusters are fine. Could be an older sidecar image in eu-west nodes still running the previous envoy config that strips unrecognized headers.
sasha: another hypothesis: the gateway uses the open-telemetry collector forwarding to the runtime through gRPC, and we might be translating to otlp and losing the original traceparent because collector is configured to generate new trace ids. 
juan: good point. If collector has "preserve_existing_trace" toggled off it will start new traces. Check collector config for resource/processor settings.
maya: collector config excerpt from eu-west: 
```
processors:
  batch:
  memory_limiter:
  attributes:
    actions:
      - action: insert
        key: service.name
        value: trace-gateway
exporters:
  otlp:
    endpoint: runtime-observability:4317
# no explicit id preservation flags
```
maya: not seeing preserve flags.
liam: In otel collector, span id/traces are preserved by default unless you explicitly modify them, but some exporters (or receiver->exporter conversion) can inject new trace ids. Are we converting protocol from HTTP to OTLP and mapping W3C traceparent incorrectly?
sasha: Also remember we have our SDKs instrumented with OpenTelemetry auto-instrumentation (go/java) at runtime. If the incoming context is missing, runtime will start a fresh root span. That would explain the mismatch.
juan: short-term mitigation: set the gateway to copy W3C trace headers into x-b3 and x-otlp headers before any processing, so nothing relies on header name. Example Lua filter snippet we used before: 
```
-- lua header copy
local tp = ngx.var.http_traceparent
if tp then ngx.req.set_header("x-b3-traceid", tp) end
```
juan: long-term: fix the collector config and ensure W3C traceparent is honored across the translation boundary.
maya: Agree. Also we should push a tweak: for high-latency requests (>500ms) we want to force full-trace capture regardless of sampling. Right now sampling at gateway is 5% which misses most tail events.
liam: sampling change has cost implications — at 200k qps, going from 5% to 100% full traces temporarily will increase storage/ingestion ~20x. But we can do dynamic tail-sampling: only sample traces where duration > threshold using the collector's tail_sampling processor.
sasha: we already have tail_sampling enabled in us-west but not eu-west. Maybe that's the reason eu-west misses tail traces.
maya: action items: 1) Juan to add header copy at gateway as stopgap (x-b3/x-otlp/x-cloud). 2) Liam to verify collector config and enable tail_sampling in eu-west. 3) Sasha to add a short-lived debug rule to always capture traces for requests tagged model=redwood-jumbo where p99 > 600ms. 4) Maya to link affected request ids to Prometheus metrics for cross-correlation.
juan: I'll open a small PR for the Lua header copy and a canary for 2 nodes in eu-west. PR will reference this thread.
liam: I'll diff collector configs across regions and push tail_sampling into the eu-west collectors. If we can't ship quickly, I'll add a temporary env var in the gateway to forward trace headers intact.
sasha: For observability dashboards: we should add a trace coverage panel in Grafana (traces per 1k requests by region) and an indicator of trace/span correlation rate with request logs. Will draft a panel.
maya: Also important: correlate GPU allocation logs (node_gpu_id) into spans so we can see whether specific GPU hosts are contributing to tail. Runtime span attribute suggestion: gpu_id, model, seq_len, batch_size. Can we have runtime teams add that?
liam: runtime already exposes gpu_id in logs; we can add as span attributes in the runtime auto-instrumentation patch I have queued.
juan: small note: AWS ALB http2 -> backend conversions can mangle headers with underscores; use hyphens for all header keys. We'll ensure our header copy uses hyphenated names.
monitoring-bot: INFO: Created incident #INC-4439 (eu-west trace loss) and attached p99 graphs.
ops-bot: FYI: rolling restart might be needed for collector config to pick new tail_sampling settings. Schedule window?
maya: let's aim for a quick canary change within the 30m fix window, then full rollout in the 2-hour maintenance window if green.
juan: PR opened: https://git.internal/redwood/gateway/pull/5123 — includes Lua header copy + unit tests. Can we merge and roll to 2 canary pods?
sasha: approve from me once CI passes. I'll prep Grafana panel and a quick dashboard alert to ensure trace coverage rises in eu-west.
liam: after we verify header preservation and tail sampling, we should run a small load test with injected artificial delays to confirm trace continuity across gateway->collector->runtime.
maya: thanks everyone. I'll post an update in ~45m with initial observations. :thumbsup:
